name: Arts AlUla and Desert X AlUla
funding: Arts AlUla sits inside the Royal Commission for AlUla, a Saudi government agency overseen by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. US nonprofit Desert Biennial produces Desert X AlUla with it.
watch: Three Desert X board members resigned in October 2019, citing Saudi human rights abuses and the Khashoggi killing. MaddocksBrown Foundation, a donor, withdrew its support.
why_flagged: Arts AlUla sits inside the Royal Commission for AlUla, a Saudi government agency overseen by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. US nonprofit Desert Biennial produces Desert X AlUla with it.
records_note: Arts AlUla posts nothing; the Royal Commission has 2023 and 2024 annual reports, and Desert Biennial files Form 990s, names donors and lists a board.

name: Misk Art Institute
funding: Subsidiary of the Mohammed bin Salman Foundation (Misk), a non-profit the Crown Prince founded in 2011. No budget or donor list found on its site.
watch: Founded December 2017; Ahmed Mater was its director then. Its summer 2026 show at Prince Faisal bin Fahd Arts Hall has over 40 works.
why_flagged: Subsidiary of the Mohammed bin Salman Foundation (Misk), a non-profit the Crown Prince founded in 2011. No budget or donor list found on its site.
records_note: The Institute posts no reports or board; its parent Misk Foundation lists annual reports for 2019 to 2024, and no accounts or donors are published.

name: National Museum of Iraq
funding: Run by Iraq's tourism and antiquities ministry. The US paid about $9M of the 2011 renovation, per its deputy director. Italy equipped its labs in 2015; France sponsored a show.
watch: In 2009 five Iraqi archaeologists wrote an open letter against a sudden reopening; the minister then removed Amira Edan as State Board of Antiquities head.
why_flagged: Run by Iraq's tourism and antiquities ministry. The US paid about $9M of the 2011 renovation, per its deputy director. Italy equipped its labs in 2015; France sponsored a show.
records_note: Its site lists no reports, accounts, donors or board, and the ministry that runs it blocked page fetches.

name: National Museum of Damascus
funding: Its parent body, the Directorate-General of Antiquities and Museums, partners UNESCO's 2025 project: initial budget $175,000, no donor named. No museum budget is published.
watch: Closed 7 December 2024 after the fall of Damascus and reopened 8 January 2025. Wikipedia reports six Roman statues stolen in a November 2025 break-in.
records_note: The parent Directorate-General of Antiquities and Museums publishes no annual reports, accounts, donors or board; it is tied to the Minister of Culture.

name: Dar al-Athar al-Islamiyyah
funding: Manages the al-Sabah Collection, on permanent loan to Kuwait under its National Council for Culture, Arts and Letters. Sponsors: KIPCO, Kuwait Petroleum Corporation and subsidiaries, Kuwait Finance House.
watch: Founded 1983. The collection holds over 30,000 objects, collected by Sheikh Nasser Sabah al-Ahmed al-Sabah. Sheikha Hussa Sabah Al-Salem Al-Sabah is director general.
why_flagged: Manages the al-Sabah Collection, on permanent loan to Kuwait under its National Council for Culture, Arts and Letters. Sponsors: KIPCO, Kuwait Petroleum Corporation and subsidiaries, Kuwait Finance House.
records_note: It posts no reports or accounts; its sponsors page names donors and sponsors without a date, and no board roster is named.

name: National Museum of Oman
funding: State museum set up by Royal Decree 62/2013. The Minister of Heritage and Tourism chairs its Board of Trustees.
watch: Its site describes it as a legal entity with financial and administrative independence. It shows Oman's heritage from earliest settlement to the present.
why_flagged: State museum set up by Royal Decree 62/2013. The Minister of Heritage and Tourism chairs its Board of Trustees. It lists no sponsors or budget.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts or sponsors; its board of trustees page names six members, led by the Minister of Heritage and Tourism.

name: Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts
funding: Patrons by tier, logos dated May 2024 to Aug 2025: Diamond UAE Ministry of Culture and Youth, Hikma, Jordan Bromine; Platinum Barjeel, Arab Potash; Gold Shoman Foundation; Silver Jordan Phosphate Mines, Jordan Petroleum Refinery, Jordan Kuwait Bank; Bronze four banks, Kemapco.
watch: Flags rest on the UAE ministry, a Gulf state body at Diamond tier, and the state-owned Jordan Petroleum Refinery. The Shoman Foundation is Arab Bank's; its 2014 US terror-financing verdict, settled 2015 and overturned 2018, is a B-level controversy outside the flags.
why_flagged: Patrons by tier, logos dated May 2024 to Aug 2025: Diamond UAE Ministry of Culture and Youth, Hikma, Jordan Bromine; Platinum Barjeel, Arab Potash; Gold Shoman Foundation; Silver Jordan Phosphate Mines, Jordan Petroleum Refinery, Jordan Kuwait Bank; Bronze four banks, Kemapco.
records_note: The gallery names patrons by tier on a partners page, undated, and its trustees on the about page; it publishes no reports or accounts.

name: Amman Design Week
funding: Founded 2016 by Queen Rania; organised with Greater Amman Municipality. 2016 sponsors: Al Manaseer Group, Zain, Aramex, Al Markaziya. 2026: Sukhtian Foundation backs the student exhibition.
watch: 2016 sponsors were Al Manaseer Group, Zain, Aramex and Al Markaziya. The 2026 edition runs 2 to 17 October across Amman and Aqaba.
records_note: ammandesignweek.com returned HTTP 403, so nothing could be checked from its own pages.

name: The Freedom Theatre
funding: 2013 annual report names Ford Foundation, Sida, AFAC, Medico International and the European Commission. British Council gave £74,976 in 2022, per the Jewish Chronicle. No current donor list.
watch: Staff told Al Jazeera that Israeli forces raided it in December 2023 and arrested two directors. Co-founder Juliano Mer-Khamis was shot dead in 2011.
records_note: The theatre posts annual reports for 2007 to 2013 and 2020, names donors in the 2013 report, lists its board, and publishes no accounts.

name: Art Encounters Foundation
funding: Founded 2015 by developer Ovidiu Șandor, who provides the building. The 2025 biennial had main partner Ploom, Japan Tobacco's heated-tobacco brand, plus Banca Transilvania, Catena and Timișoara municipality funding.
watch: Runs the Art Encounters Biennial (2015 to 2025). A museum-standard venue in the former Casa ISHO opens in September 2026 with a Picasso show.
why_flagged: Founded 2015 by developer Ovidiu Șandor, who provides the building. The 2025 biennial had main partner Ploom, Japan Tobacco's heated-tobacco brand, plus Banca Transilvania, Catena and Timișoara municipality funding.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts or funder list, only a count of 50 partners; the team page names the president but no board.

name: National Museum of Contemporary Art (MNAC)
funding: Romanian Ministry of Culture funds it, including RON 500,000 for 2024 acquisitions. Sponsors include AQUA Carpatica, Greentek Lighting, Crama Oprișor, Molotow, UniCredit Bank and BRD Groupe Société Générale.
watch: Opened 2004 inside the Palace of the Parliament. ArtMargins writer Augustin Ioan said in 2008 that Prime Minister Nastase financed it in secret.
records_note: Its Partners and Sponsors page shows logos only; no annual reports, accounts or board list are posted, only ministry orders on its regulations.

name: Sofia City Art Gallery
funding: Sofia Municipality funds yearly acquisitions, resumed in 2007. Partners listed: Ministry of Culture, America for Bulgaria Foundation, Aurubis Bulgaria, Institut français and Goethe-Institut. No budget is published.
watch: Founded 1928 as part of Sofia's city museum. Holds more than 23,000 works by Bulgarian artists.
records_note: Its Partners page shows six unlabelled partner logos and media logos; no annual reports, accounts or board are posted, only a staff list.
